comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## RECURRENCE — and this time the root cause is identified, not just the symptom

review-bot went down again and stayed down ~59 minutes, silently. I restored it manually. But the
important part is *why* it did not come back on its own, which this ticket previously did not have.

### Root cause: `unless-stopped` plus a clean exit is a permanent outage

```
docker inspect -f '{{.HostConfig.RestartPolicy.Name}}':
  compose-review-bot-1   unless-stopped
  compose-opcert-1       unless-stopped
  compose-gerrit-1       unless-stopped

docker ps -a  (before my intervention):
  compose-review-bot-1 | Exited (0) 59 minutes ago      <-- clean exit, code 0
  rebar-mcp-...        | Up About a minute (healthy)
  compose-opcert-1     | Up About a minute
  compose-gerrit-1     | Up About a minute
```

`unless-stopped` means "restart it unless it was **explicitly stopped**." review-bot exited with
**code 0** — a clean, voluntary exit — and Docker therefore treated it as intentionally stopped and
declined to restart it, including across the host reboot that brought every other container back.

So this is not a flaky container or a crash loop. It is a policy that is *correct* for a service a
human stops on purpose, and *wrong* for a service whose absence silently disables the merge gate.
The other three containers came back precisely because they had not exited cleanly first.

**Consequence, stated plainly: with review-bot down there is no source of `LLM-Review` votes, so no
change can satisfy the two-vote gate and nothing can merge.** For 59 minutes the project's merge path
was closed and nothing said so.

### The reboot was deliberate and external — not a crash

Worth recording so this is not misfiled as instability:

```
Sep 06 02:40:41 systemd-logind: Power key pressed short.
Sep 06 02:40:42 systemd-logind: Powering off...
Sep 06 02:41:11 systemd-logind: Failed to get load state of poweroff.target: Connection timed out
Sep 06 02:41:12 systemd-logind: Failed to execute poweroff operation: Connection timed out
Sep 06 02:41:16 systemd-logind: Power key pressed short.        <-- second press needed
       host back up 02:43,  `uptime` = 0 min,  EC2 status checks ok throughout
```

An ACPI power-button event (an EC2 API reboot), not an OOM or panic. Note the shutdown itself
**hung** and required a second press — consistent with the loaded host, and worth remembering as a
symptom to expect during future maintenance.

During the window Gerrit was fully unreachable at TCP level (`HTTP=000`, connect timeout at 45s and
100s; `git ls-remote` killed at 90s). It recovered on its own: root now answers **HTTP 200 in 0.50s**
and `ls-remote` returns in **2s**.

### Two incidental findings from the same logs

1. **Probe truncation confirmed from the host's own mouth**, corroborating the metric-side analysis:
   `rebar-health: probe exit report: SERVICE_RESULT=timeout EXIT_CODE=killed EXIT_STATUS=TERM
   probe_truncated=1`.
2. **A duplicate `Change-Id` is breaking the review bot for one change.** Its reconcile loop logs:
   `HTTP 404: Multiple changes found for I266870f28c4935ad009ceff3d9c32479cb2c7988`. That is the
   failure mode `git commit --amend -m/-F` produces (it drops the trailer, the hook stamps a fresh
   one, and a duplicate change opens). The bot cannot resolve the id, so it cannot vote on that
   change — worth its own ticket if it is not already tracked.

### Suggested direction (not a decision)

`unless-stopped` -> `always` for review-bot would fix the specific gap, but on its own it converts a
silent outage into a possible crash loop, so it needs pairing with an actual liveness check on the
*vote-casting capability* rather than on the process. The deeper issue this ticket already names is
that autodeploy reported "up to date" while the service was down: a deploy check that inspects
desired-vs-actual image state, and not whether the container is running and voting, will keep
reporting green through exactly this failure.

No Gerrit git data was touched and Gerrit itself was not restarted.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RCA so far: observation: review-bot was process-healthy and /health returned 200 while Gerrit authentication paths needed for vote casting were returning 401. Working comparison: after resetting the Gerrit service account HTTP password to the SSM token, /a/accounts/self and /a/plugins/events-log/events/ returned 200 and the same bot process could vote on change 2801. Hypothesis confirmed: the secret rotation updated SSM/container .env but did not leave Gerrit's service-account HTTP password and the rendered refs/meta/config webhook secret in sync with that token; the health endpoint only checked process liveness/queue counters, not Gerrit auth/vote-casting capability. Fix direction implemented in worktree blackfly-healthcheck: /health now performs a bounded Gerrit auth probe and returns 503 degraded on auth failure.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

`rebar-autodeploy` reports `"up to date; no-op"` while declared services are DEAD. On 2026-09-05 the
`review-bot` and `opcert` containers exited at a host power cycle and stayed down for **24 minutes**
across at least twelve autodeploy runs, every one of which logged success.

`LLM-Review` votes stopped landing for every session during that window. Nothing detected it; it was
found by hand while investigating why three changes sat at `Verified +1` with no LLM vote.

## Observed

```
docker ps -a
  rebar-mcp-1d60c5f72ff0-8092   Up 20 minutes (healthy)
  compose-gerrit-1              Up 22 minutes
  compose-review-bot-1          Exited (127) 24 minutes ago     <-- DOWN
  compose-opcert-1              Exited (127) 24 minutes ago     <-- DOWN

journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy (runs every ~2 min, exit 0 each time)
  {"event":"autodeploy","msg":"mcp reconcile: swept orphan mcp images (removed=0 kept-live+prev=1)"}
  {"event":"autodeploy","msg":"up to date (1d60c5f72ff008ddc3acdff42fd5b84ecdfb2752); no-op"}
```

Recovery was a manual `docker start compose-review-bot-1 compose-opcert-1`; both came back
immediately and the bot resumed accepting webhooks (`POST /webhook 202`, `GET /health 200`).

## The defect

Autodeploy's liveness question is **"is the deployed SHA current?"**, not **"are the declared
services running?"**. Those diverge exactly when it matters. It also reconciles only the `mcp`
image — `review-bot` and `opcert` have no reconcile path at all, so nothing was even looking.

This is the session's recurring shape: a check that runs, reports success, and is silent about the
property it exists to protect. Siblings: `erratic-sunny-genet` (Mirror Guard reports
`healthy:false` when it could not reach the host), `deistic-conventual-blackmamba` (CI votes
`Verified-1 FAILURE` on a cancelled run), `satirical-baryte-cat` (worktree GC hangs inside its own
lock and every later run SKIPs).

## Why it matters for stability specifically

The system's three services are Gerrit, the rebar MCP server, and the code-review bot. Two of the
three can be down indefinitely with the deploy mechanism reporting healthy. No alarm covers this:
the review bot has no liveness metric, so its absence is not a missing-data condition either — it
is simply invisible.

## Note on exit 127

Both containers exited **127**. The logs before death show the review bot failing to clone from the
Gerrit it SHARES A HOST WITH (`RPC failed; curl 28 Operation too slow. Less than 1000 bytes/sec`)
and a tracker write timing out under lock contention. Whether 127 is an ungraceful-termination
artifact of the power cycle or a genuine entrypoint fault is NOT established — worth determining,
because those need different fixes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1 Autodeploy detects a declared-but-not-running service and says so, distinctly from a
      SHA-currency no-op.
- [x] AC2 It either restarts such a service or fails loudly. Decide and RECORD which; silently
      restarting a container that is crash-looping is its own failure mode.
- [x] AC3 `review-bot` and `opcert` have a reconcile path, or a recorded reason they do not.
- [x] AC4 A liveness signal exists for the review bot such that its absence is detectable — today
      it is invisible rather than merely unmeasured.
- [x] AC5 Both branches proven: a healthy deployment still no-ops quietly; a dead service is
      reported.

## Constraints

Never use `--force` or any gate bypass. `timeout` does not exist on this macOS host (exit 127) —
bound with `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'`. Terraform apply is operator-authorized and must follow a
reviewed plan. Do not touch the shared main checkout; do not `git stash`.
